body.en: Circle theorems and coordinate geometry of conic sections are significant topics on the EST II Mathematics subject test.
Write the equation of a circle with centre \( (3,-2) \) and radius 5. \[ (x-3)^2+(y+2)^2=25. \]

body.en:
Ellipses and hyperbolas

An ellipse: \( \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1 \). A hyperbola: \( \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1 \). EST II may ask you to identify the type of conic from a standard-form equation and state key features like vertices, foci, or asymptotes.

Circle equation: \((x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\). A tangent to a circle at point \(P\) is perpendicular to the radius at \(P\). Circle theorems: angle at centre = twice angle at circumference; angles in same segment are equal; tangent-radius angle = 90°. Chord perpendicular bisector passes through the centre.

label.en: Worked example — Tangent from external point

body.en:
A circle has centre \(O(3,2)\) and radius 5. Point \(P(10,2)\) lies outside the circle. Find the length of the tangent from \(P\) to the circle.

\(OP = \sqrt{(10-3)^2+(2-2)^2} = 7\). Tangent length \(= \sqrt{OP^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{49-25} = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\).

caption.en: Ellipse centered at \((1, -2)\) with horizontal major axis length \(2a = 8\) and vertical minor axis length \(2b = 6\). The foci lie at \((1 \pm \sqrt{7}, -2)\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Circles & Conic Sections

body.en:
• Completing the Square for Circles: When converting general form \(x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\) to standard form \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), remember to add \((D/2)^2\) and \((E/2)^2\) to both sides of the equation. Forgetting to add them to the right-hand side produces an incorrect radius.
  • Tangent Perpendicularity: A line tangent to a circle at point \(P(x_1, y_1)\) is always perpendicular to the radius \(OP\). If the radius has slope \(m\), the tangent line has slope \(-1/m\).
  • Conic Identification from General Quadratic: In \(Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\): if \(A = C\), it is a circle; if \(A \neq C\) but both have the same sign (\(AC > 0\)), it is an ellipse; if \(A\) and \(C\) have opposite signs (\(AC < 0\)), it is a hyperbola; if either \(A = 0\) or \(C = 0\) (but not both), it is a parabola.
  • Focal Distance Formulas: For an ellipse, \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) (foci are inside the ellipse, so \(c < a\)). For a hyperbola, \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) (foci are outside the vertices, so \(c > a\)). Do not confuse these two relations!

question.en: Find the equation of the circle that passes through \((0,0)\), \((6,0)\) and \((0,8)\).
Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) at the point \(P(3, 4)\).

solution.en:
Radius slope: The center is the origin \(O(0, 0)\). The slope of the radius connecting \((0, 0)\) and \((3, 4)\) is \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \dfrac{4 - 0}{3 - 0} = \dfrac{4}{3}. \]

Tangent line slope: Since the tangent is perpendicular to the radius, its slope is the negative reciprocal: \[ m_{\text{tangent}} = -\dfrac{3}{4}. \]

Point-slope equation: Using point \(P(3, 4)\): \[ y - 4 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 3) \implies 4(y - 4) = -3(x - 3) \implies 4y - 16 = -3x + 9 \implies 3x + 4y = 25. \]
